---
title: "Use Suppose from the terminal"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 144
)
library(suppose)
```

The command-line interface calls the same record and numerical operations as
the R API. It is useful for inspecting bundles and producing reproducible JSON
without opening the workbench.

## Install a launcher

With Suppose installed in your R library, choose a directory on your shell's
`PATH`:

```{r launcher, eval=FALSE}
suppose::install_suppose_cli(destdir = "~/bin")
```

For an isolated environment, the external [ir launcher](https://r-lib.github.io/ir/tools.html)
can install from an authenticated clone:

```sh
ir tool install "local::$(pwd)"
```

The UI additionally requires the development packages described in the
[workbench setup](workbench.html#installation).

## Create and inspect a worked example

```sh
suppose demo example.json --seed 47
suppose inspect example.json
suppose inspect example.json --json
```

`demo` refuses an existing destination. `inspect` works for qualitative records
as well as numerical ones, including judgments, model references, and retained
research designs.

## Calculate without changing the bundle

```sh
suppose predict example.json --seed 47 --n 4000 > predictions.json
```

Prediction requires an explicit seed and writes a separate JSON result. It does
not modify the input record. JSON goes to standard output, diagnostics go to
standard error, and failures return a nonzero exit status. A qualitative record
without a numerical candidate cannot be used for `predict`.

Use `suppose --help` for commands and `suppose observe --help` for observation
import options. The [measurement guide](measurements.html) explains source,
exposure, and intended-use declarations.
